name: HateCheck
description: Detecting online hate is a difficult task that even state-of-the-art models struggle with. Typically, hate speech detection models are evaluated by measuring their performance on held-out test data using metrics such as accuracy and F1 score. However, this approach makes it difficult to identify specific model weak points.
typical_sota_score: 70–90% (varies substantially by test slice; many models perform well on aggregate but fail on targeted functional tests)
reputation: Widely used as a diagnostic benchmark for probing specific failure modes in hate speech detection rather than just aggregate performance.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on targeted behavioral tests; useful for robustness and bias analysis, with scores depending heavily on the subset and label setup.
